decisions.rationale: The phrase 'Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy' refers to two separate diseases (Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Becker muscular dystrophy) and splitting it would lose information, so it is one contiguous Composite Mention.

The repeated phrase 'Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy' in the abstract body is a second, separate mention of the two diseases and is annotated as a Composite Mention because duplicate mentions are all annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §2 (Composite Mention); §4 (Annotate duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'DMD' in parentheses is the abbreviation for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a single specific disease, so it is annotated as its own mention as a synonymous abbreviation.
'BMD' in parentheses is the abbreviation for Becker muscular dystrophy, a single specific disease, so it is annotated as its own mention as a synonymous abbreviation.
Here 'DMD' names the gene ('the DMD gene') rather than the disease, so it does not refer to a disease mention and is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated); What NOT to Annotate §4 (non-disease references)

decisions.rationale: 'particularly in DMD' refers to the disease Duchenne muscular dystrophy as the setting of the deletions, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
'specific to DMD' refers to the disease Duchenne muscular dystrophy as a standalone referent, not as a modifier of another noun, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
'to BMD' refers to the disease Becker muscular dystrophy as a standalone referent in 'Deletions specific to DMD and to BMD', so it is a Specific Disease mention.
In 'Half of all BMD patients', BMD is a disease name used to modify the noun 'patients', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
'the more severe DMD' refers to Duchenne muscular dystrophy as the disease produced by smaller deletions, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
